evidence.text: In 1983, Thatcher convened a seminar at Chequers with experts to reassess the West's approach to the Soviet Union. This strategic gathering laid the intellectual groundwork for her eventual diplomatic engagement with Soviet leadership, notably Mikhail Gorbachev. Thatcher argued that studying adversaries is essential because it creates strategic openings to eventually transform hostile relationships into cooperative ones. Strategic intelligence and deep comprehension of an adversary are prerequisites for diplomatic breakthroughs and long-term conflict resolution. Thoroughly knowing the enemy enables the eventual transformation of geopolitical adversaries into partners.
